notes.claim: Sulphation occurs when a lead acid battery is deprived of a full charge.
Capacity test is the only way to get an accurate value for the battery's actual capacity.
IEEE 450 and IEEE 1188 recommend replacing a battery whose capacity is below 80 per cent of the manufacturer's rating, as a test-equipment maker reports.
Sources give different impedance-drift thresholds linked to about 80 per cent capacity or a baseline-based warning: 20, 30 to 50, 50 and 150 per cent.
notes.contested: Megger finds a 20 per cent impedance rise in flooded cells generally matches 80 per cent capacity; an EPRI study found most cells below 80 per cent at 150 per cent of nominal impedance; Battcon tips flag 30-50 per cent from baseline; an NRC report uses over 50 per cent for VRLA cells.

notes.claim: Prolonged overcharge contributes to grid corrosion.
A single resistance-based reading predicts state of health little better than a coin toss, about 5 right in 10 (added for i7).
In one example of trended impedance, the first ten or eleven readings looked fine and then a steady upward trend showed (added for i7).
In a stratified cell the acid concentrates at the bottom, starving the upper half of the cell (added for i7).
Stratification occurs when a battery dwells at low charge, below 80 per cent, never receives a full charge and has shallow discharges (added for i7).
Under prolonged charge deprivation, soft lead sulphate turns into stable crystals deposited on the negative plates (added for i7).
Grid corrosion happens mainly on the grid, as a softening and shedding of the lead off the plates (added for i7).
Sulphation can be reversed if serviced in time, but corrosion is permanent (added for i7).
In a valve-regulated cell, excess charging causes gassing, venting, then water loss and dry-out (added for i7).
A capacity test on a new battery, as part of its acceptance test, gives the baseline later tests are compared with (added for i7).
An equalising charge helps reverse stratification by mixing the electrolyte through electrolysis (added for i7).
